extracted.intended_audience: attorneys registered to practice before the USPTO; Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff; parties to USPTO disciplinary settlements
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evaluative criteria for approving a Proposed Settlement Agreement resolving disciplinary charges against a registered patent attorney, including jurisdictional basis, required stipulated facts and legal conclusions, applicable regulatory citations, and the range of sanctions/notifications ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed Settlement Agreement must satisfy 37 C.F.R. § 11.26
rubrics_metrics.description: The Proposed Settlement Agreement must set forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions and satisfy the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states: 'The Proposed Settlement Agreement, which satisfies the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.26, resolves all disciplinary tiction by the United States Patent and Trademark Office ("USPTO" or "Office") arising from the stipulated facts set forth below.' It must be submitted to the USPTO Director (or his designate) for approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction — practitioner subject to USPTO disciplinary rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A person registered to practice before the USPTO is subject to the Disciplinary Rules of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility (e.g., 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.) and to statutory/regulatory provisions cited (35 U.S.C. § 32; 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.26, 11.59).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order establishes jurisdiction by noting: 'At all times relevant hereto, Respondent ... has been registered as an attorney to practice before the USPTO and is subject to the Disciplinary Rules ... set forth at 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.' Use registration number and admission information to show coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-bar discipline as basis for USPTO discipline (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via § 10.23(c)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Being disciplined on ethical grounds by a State Bar may constitute a violation of USPTO disciplinary rules and provide grounds for discipline by the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) (via § 10.23(c)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Respondent 'acknowledges that his conduct violated 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5) by being disciplined on ethical grounds by the Supreme Court of Florida.' A prior state disciplinary sanction (e.g., public reprimand) is a relevant predicate for USPTO action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipulated facts must recount factual and procedural background
rubrics_metrics.description: The stipulated facts in a settlement should include factual antecedents to the state-bar complaint and the procedural history (e.g., filing of complaint, settlement/plea, referee finding, court approval).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example content from the Order: respondent's registration number and admission date; description of the Florida Bar complaint (agreement restricting employee competition); the Conditional Guilty Plea and Consent Judgment for Discipline; referee's finding; and Supreme Court of Florida approval directing public reprimand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal conclusions in settlement acknowledging specific rule violations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Proposed Settlement Agreement should include legal conclusions in which the respondent acknowledges which USPTO rules were violated and why, citing specific regulatory provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case the Agreement and Final Order contain an acknowledgment that 'his conduct violated 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5).' Such acknowledgments tie stipulated facts to regulatory violations and support the proposed sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate sanction — public reprimand
rubrics_metrics.description: One sanction available and here imposed is a public reprimand for a registered patent attorney found to have violated the disciplinary rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states: 'Respondent be, and hereby is, publicly reprimanded.' Use of a public reprimand may be appropriate where the respondent has already been disciplined by a state bar and the parties have agreed to this sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order and a Notice in the Official Gazette describing the reprimand, the respondent (including registration number), the regulation violated, and the basis (e.g., prior state-bar reprimand).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs: 'The OED Director shall publish this Final Order; The OED Director shall publish the following Notice in the Official Gazette' and provides sample Notice text that names the respondent, registration number, rule violated, and statutory/regulatory authority (35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.26 and 11.59).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to disciplinary enforcement agencies, courts, and the public
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice of public discipline and reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order requires dissemination beyond the Official Gazette: 'The OED Director shall give notice of public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted to practice, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and the public.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs — parties bear their own costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The settlement may provide that each party shall bear its own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order specifies: 'The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.' This is an explicit cost-allocation term that may be part of settlements.
